sections.title: General chat, small
sections.line: Assistants under 10 billion parameters. By the app's estimate, the smallest version of each needs 0.5 to 12 GB of GPU memory.

sections.title: General chat, medium
sections.line: Assistants of 10 to 40 billion parameters. By the app's estimate, the smallest version of each needs 8.5 to 34.8 GB of GPU memory.

sections.title: General chat, large
sections.line: Assistants of 40 to 150 billion parameters. By the app's estimate, the smallest version of each needs 74.6 to 132 GB of GPU memory.

sections.title: General chat, very large
sections.line: The largest open models, over 150 billion parameters. By the app's estimate, the smallest version of each needs 128.2 to 1,776 GB of GPU memory, so they need several data-center GPUs.

sections.title: Coding and math
sections.line: Models trained to write and fix code, or to solve math problems.

sections.title: Vision and multimodal
sections.line: Models built to answer questions about images, video or audio as well as text.

sections.title: Documents and OCR
sections.line: Models that read scanned pages, PDFs, tables and charts into text, Markdown or structured data.

sections.title: Security research
sections.line: Models for offensive and defensive security work. Those marked as refusal-removed answer requests their originals decline.

sections.title: Refusals removed
sections.line: General models whose publishers removed the refusals, so they answer requests the originals decline.

sections.title: Speech to text
sections.line: Models that transcribe speech, some with timestamps, speaker labels or translation.

sections.title: Text to speech
sections.line: Models that read text aloud, some in a voice cloned from a short sample.

sections.title: Image generation
sections.line: Models that make and edit images from a text prompt.

sections.title: Video generation
sections.line: Models that make short videos from a text prompt or a still image.

sections.title: Embeddings and reranking
sections.line: Models that turn text or images into vectors for search, and rerankers that score how well a passage answers a query.

sections.title: Audio and music
sections.line: Models that make music or label sounds.

sections.title: Computer vision
sections.line: Models that classify images, find and outline objects, estimate depth or build 3D scenes.

sections.title: Robotics
sections.line: Vision-language-action models that turn camera images and instructions into robot actions or plans.

sections.title: Text tools and decision models
sections.line: Models for one task: summaries, translation, sentiment, question answering, or a typed decision such as yes or no, a choice or a rating.

sections.title: Science and forecasting
sections.line: Models for DNA, protein sequences and time series.
